newsitem.title: USA: UPS to press White House on intervention.
newsitem.headline: UPS to press White House on intervention.

text.p: The chief labour negotiator for United Parcel Service said Monday that the strike-bound company would press the Clinton administration to intervene in a nationwide Teamsters walkout.

Shortly after President Clinton ruled out the idea of White House involvement, UPS negotiator Dave Murray said the company expected to talk to administration officials later in the day. "We're disappointed, of course, and we'll keep pressing the administration for further consideration," Murray told reporters in a conference call.

But the world's largest package delivery company gave no indication that it would back down from its final offer to the Teamsters union, which represents 185,000 UPS employees, or nearly two-thirds of its U.S. work force.
Asked if the company was resolved not to budge from its last position, Murray answered: "That's fair to say, yes."

The walkout by union drivers, loaders and package sorters began at 12:01 EDT (0401 GMT) Monday after a last-ditch effort to set a new five-year contract in Washington collapsed over differences on pay, benefits and job security.

About 12 hours later, UPS said an overwhelming number of Teamster members had joined the strike, leaving a skeleton crew of managers and non-union workers to staff what operations they could. A company spokesman said a number of union members -- "in the low thousands" -- had decided to cross picket lines and said some entire facilities were operating normally.
